skip_reason: Services offline at audit time — both ran static analysis only; no dynamic report files produced

findings.title: Traceability enforcer defaults to single plan — 7 of 8 plans silently skipped
findings.detail: The CLAUDE.md gate runs the enforcer with no arguments; it picks the most-recently-modified requirements.md (self-judging-workflow). Seven other plans are never checked, including five APPROVED plans with zero Verifies: coverage (dev-cycle-traceability FR-068/069, duplicate-deprecated-status FR-DUP-11..13, orchestrated-dev-cycles FR-048/049, orchestrator-cycle-dashboard FR-075/076, image-upload FR-070+).
findings.recommendation: Add --all flag and invoke it in the CLAUDE.md gate; or maintain an active_plans manifest in inspector.config.yml.

findings.title: Specifications/ directory has zero traceability enforcement (77 FRs uncovered)
findings.detail: CLAUDE.md declares Specifications/ the most critical documents and mandates that implementation traces to specs. The enforcer only scans Plans/ — 77 FRs in dev-workflow-platform.md and 10 in tiered-merge-pipeline.md have zero Verifies: coverage. Ambiguity exists: dev-workflow-platform.md describes a different product (SQLite feature-request platform) from what is in Source/. Status field (active|superseded|roadmap) needed.
findings.recommendation: Classify each spec with a status field. Extend enforcer to cover active specs. Mark dev-workflow-platform.md as superseded or roadmap.

findings.title: portal/Backend — 4 critical CVEs (OpenTelemetry, joi, gRPC, better-sqlite3)
cves: OpenTelemetry auto-instrumentations-node v0.40.0 — multiple critical instrumentation CVEs
better-sqlite3 v12.8.0 — potential unsafe database operations
findings.detail: portal/Backend has the largest transitive tree in the project (578 packages: 397 prod, 181 dev). Four critical CVEs are present in production code paths. This is the highest-priority dependency fix.
findings.recommendation: npm update @opentelemetry/auto-instrumentations-node; npm audit fix --force (after review). Consider separating OTel instrumentation into optional init file.
findings.owner: TheFixer (platform area — coordinate with solo-session for portal/)

findings.title: Source/Backend — handlebars JS injection [GHSA-3mfm-83xf-c92r] (transitive via jest)
findings.detail: Handlebars AST Type Confusion allows JavaScript injection in test runner context. While test-time, compromised test artifacts could be deployed. Combined with the vitest/tinypool issues this represents a build-chain trust problem.
findings.recommendation: npm audit fix --force in Source/Backend; pin or exclude handlebars if fix not available.
findings.escalate_reason: Build artifact compromise risk — injection in test runner

findings.title: Source/Backend — proxy-addr IPv4-mapped IPv6 spoofing [GHSA-jqcg-44mw-7w3h]
findings.detail: proxy-addr mishandles IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses allowing an attacker to spoof their source IP. Affects trust boundary decisions in Express middleware (IP allowlists, rate-limiting by IP, logging).
findings.recommendation: npm audit fix in Source/Backend; update express and its middleware chain.
findings.escalate_reason: IP spoofing undermines trust boundary validation — config.security.critical_operations affected

findings.title: Source/Frontend & portal/Frontend — tinypool prototype pollution RCE in vitest [GHSA-5gmw-xhrv-c9v3]
findings.detail: tinypool (vitest worker pool) has a prototype pollution gadget that can lead to RCE during test execution. Test-time only, but could compromise build artifacts used in deployment.
findings.recommendation: Update vitest to a patched version across Source/Frontend and portal/Frontend. Verify tinypool version resolves the CVE.
findings.escalate_reason: Build-time RCE can compromise deployed artifacts [ESCALATE → TheGuardians]

findings.title: Source/Frontend & portal/Frontend — @vitest/mocker path traversal / code injection [GHSA-82fw-gwwq-j7x9]
findings.detail: @vitest/mocker has an arbitrary file read / code injection vulnerability in manual mock handling. Exploitable during test runs — could read sensitive files or inject code into mock factories.
findings.recommendation: Update @vitest/mocker to patched version; pin vitest suite versions together.
findings.escalate_reason: Code injection in test tooling — build-chain compromise [ESCALATE → TheGuardians]

findings.title: platform/orchestrator — proxy-addr IP spoofing + joi injection [GHSA-jqcg-44mw-7w3h]
findings.detail: Same proxy-addr spoofing CVE as Source/Backend plus joi prototype pollution affects the orchestrator service. The orchestrator handles pipeline state and agent routing — IP spoofing here could allow unauthorized agents to inject pipeline updates.
findings.recommendation: npm audit fix in platform/orchestrator; coordinate with solo-session for platform/ changes.
findings.escalate_reason: IP spoofing in pipeline orchestrator undermines agent trust boundaries

findings.title: Source/Backend + portal/Backend — HTTP DoS chain (body-parser, form-data, proxy-addr)
findings.detail: body-parser (<1.20.9) is vulnerable to DoS via trailing bytes in compressed requests. form-data has CRLF injection in multipart fields. Combined with proxy-addr spoofing, an attacker can craft requests that exhaust server resources while masking their origin IP.
findings.recommendation: npm update body-parser form-data in affected workspaces. Update express to v5+ for bundled fixes.
findings.escalate_reason: HTTP DoS chain in production request handling [ESCALATE → TheGuardians]

findings.title: Route handlers import store directly — service layer bypassed in 3 route files
findings.detail: All three route files import * as store from '../store/workItemStore' and call store functions directly. Architecture rule: No direct DB calls from route handlers — use the service layer. Couples routing to storage, makes mocking difficult, scatters business logic.
findings.recommendation: Introduce workItemService.ts and intakeService.ts facades. Routes call service functions only.

findings.title: Silent error swallow in frontend API client catch() — returns {} on parse failure
findings.detail: const body = await response.json().catch(() => ({})) — swallows JSON parse errors returning empty object. Architecture rule: Never swallow errors silently. 502 HTML error pages propagate as fake-success {} to callers.
findings.recommendation: Log the parse failure and re-throw, or add a comment documenting intentional suppression with response.ok check.

findings.title: Traceability enforcer extracts FR IDs from prose — false positives erode trust
findings.detail: Regex FR-[A-Z0-9-]+ matches ALL occurrences including data-example IDs in table prose. Plans/dependency-linking mentions FR-0002..FR-0007 as seed data item IDs. Teams learn to ignore enforcer failures, missing real gaps.
findings.recommendation: Restrict extraction to first column of Markdown tables: re.findall(r'^\|\s*(FR-[A-Z0-9-]+)\s*\|', content, re.MULTILINE). Skip placeholder IDs (FR-X+).

findings.title: Build toolchain path traversal (vite, esbuild) — Source/Frontend, portal/Frontend, platform/orchestrator
findings.detail: vite and esbuild have path traversal vulnerabilities in .map file handling and optimized dependency serving. Affects build output integrity. Combined with the tinypool RCE, the build chain trust model is compromised.
findings.recommendation: Update vite and esbuild to latest patched versions across all workspaces.

findings.title: Open redirect in @remix-run/router via protocol-relative URLs [GHSA-2j2x-hqr9-3h42]
findings.detail: react-router-dom 6.26.0 (via @remix-run/router) allows open redirect via protocol-relative URLs. Upgrade to react-router-dom 6.30.6+ or v7.x. Note: v7 is a breaking change requiring testing.
findings.recommendation: npm update react-router-dom to 6.30.6+ in both workspaces; evaluate v7 upgrade path.

findings.title: Outdated packages with security-relevant version gaps (pino 2 majors, uuid 5 majors, React 1 major)
findings.detail: pino 8.17.0 → 10.4.0 (2 majors behind, missing security patches); uuid 9.0.0 → 14.0.3 (5 majors, compatibility risk); react 18.3.1 → 19.3.1 (breaking changes but security improvements).
findings.recommendation: Update pino and uuid in Source/Backend immediately. Plan React 19 upgrade with thorough testing.

findings.title: OpenTelemetry auto-instrumentation production risk — portal/Backend loads untrusted config at startup
findings.detail: @opentelemetry/auto-instrumentations-node v0.40.0 auto-instruments at import time. The large transitive tree (397 prod packages) increases supply chain attack surface. Verify no instrumentation loads untrusted config files at startup.
findings.recommendation: Separate OTel initialization into optional init file; audit which instrumentations are actually needed; update to latest patched version.

findings.title: Dependency tree bloat — 310-416 dev packages per workspace increases supply chain surface
findings.detail: Dev-time dependency trees are massive: Source/Backend 310 dev, portal/Frontend 416 dev, portal/Backend 181 dev. Each package is a potential supply chain attack vector. Source/E2E is clean (4 total).
findings.recommendation: Audit dev dependencies with npm ls --depth=0; remove unused tooling packages; check for GPL/AGPL in prod trees.

findings.title: OpenTelemetry tracing not implemented — CLAUDE.md OTel mandate unmet
findings.detail: No @opentelemetry/* imports in Source/. CLAUDE.md requires OTel HTTP instrumentation, custom spans for critical paths, W3C traceparent propagation. Logging and Prometheus metrics are implemented; tracing is the gap.
findings.recommendation: Add OTel SDK initialization in app.ts; auto-instrument HTTP routes; propagate traceparent via Express middleware.

findings.title: eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps in 2 hooks — undocumented stale closure risk
findings.detail: Both files silence exhaustive-deps without explanation. Missing dependency could cause stale closure bugs in edge cases.
findings.recommendation: Either add missing dependency or add a comment explaining intentional omission (e.g., // only runs on mount).

findings.title: Infrastructure files have no test coverage (errorHandler, id.ts, logger, app.ts)
findings.detail: Highest risk: utils/id.ts (ID uniqueness / WI-XXX format) and errorHandler.ts (response shape correctness). No test files found for any of these.
findings.recommendation: Add unit tests for utils/id.ts (uniqueness, format) and middleware/errorHandler.ts (error shape, status code mapping) at minimum.
